periods.analysis: The 911 call abandonment rate finished 2024-Q3 at 4.3%, within the <=5.0% target and green for the quarter. With no prior quarter in this series, we should treat 4.3% as the operating baseline rather than a victory lap. The West Harbor PSAP pod and the Eastview overflow positions held up through summer beach traffic, with the Tuesday and Friday evening call bands still carrying the highest abandoned-call risk. From a public-trust standpoint, the result says callers are generally reaching us, but the margin is narrow enough to manage by procedure, not assumption.
periods.recommendations: Maintain the current two-pod staffing model and keep the Eastview overflow positions open during beach-event dispersal windows. Begin a weekly abandoned-call review for calls tagged ACD-ABN-1 through ACD-ABN-4, with supervisors documenting whether the caller reconnected within 90 seconds. Use the 4.3% baseline to set shift-level watch lists before the Q4 holiday and storm season schedule is finalized.

periods.analysis: The abandonment rate improved to 3.5% in 2024-Q4, down 0.8 percentage points from 4.3%, and remained green against the <=5.0% target. That movement is meaningful because it came during the holiday retail surge and the first two coastal storm watches, not during a quiet period. The call-back queue pilot on consoles HB-12 through HB-15 appears to have reduced repeat dialing, and the staggered meal relief schedule kept more call-takers logged in between 1600 and 2000 hours. This is the kind of operational gain we can acknowledge while still documenting the controls that produced it.
periods.recommendations: Keep the staggered meal-relief schedule in the standard operating plan through winter and assign it an owner on each watch. Extend the call-back queue pilot from four consoles to the full primary PSAP bank after verifying CAD interface logs with the vendor. Continue publishing the monthly abandonment summary to patrol, fire, and city leadership so the green result supports public confidence with evidence.

periods.analysis: In 2025-Q1 the rate moved to 3.8%, up 0.3 percentage points from 3.5%, while staying green and below the <=5.0% target. The increase is modest, but it lines up with January respiratory-illness absences and several weather-related school-delay mornings when call clustering was heavier than normal. The new hire cohort PSAP-25A was still in call-taking phase II, so supervisors appropriately protected quality by not overextending trainees during peak periods. The system remained reliable, and the quarter shows the difference between controlled variation and a service failure.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green performance by keeping PSAP-25A on supervised call-taking, but add two targeted simulation blocks for high-volume morning events before they move to independent status. Rebalance the Monday morning and school-delay staffing template so one trained relief call-taker is available before 0700 hours. Track abandonment separately for illness-related staffing days to confirm whether the 0.3-point increase is a staffing exposure or normal seasonal noise.

periods.analysis: The 2025-Q2 abandonment rate rose to 4.5%, up 0.7 percentage points from 3.8%, but it remained green under the <=5.0% standard. This is still acceptable performance, yet it is the closest result to the target so far and deserves watchful management. Memorial Day waterfront events, permit activity around HarborFest setup, and the Route 6 construction detour all pushed more non-emergency misdials and transfer calls into the 911 queue. The procedure held, but the buffer narrowed, which is exactly when we tighten the operating plan rather than wait for a yellow result.
periods.recommendations: Add a pre-event staffing checklist for HarborFest, waterfront races, and Route 6 detour weekends, including one additional cross-trained call-taker from 1400 to 2200 hours. Work with Communications to push the non-emergency number in event permits, vendor packets, and digital message boards so preventable calls do not enter the 911 queue. Keep the Q2 4.5% result on the command review agenda until the rate moves back below 4.0% or the seasonal surge has clearly passed.

periods.analysis: The rate improved to 4.2% in 2025-Q3, down 0.3 percentage points from 4.5%, and remained green against the <=5.0% target. That improvement suggests the Q2 event controls and non-emergency messaging had some effect during the heaviest visitor period. Crews supporting the HarborFest command post reported fewer transfer loops from event security, and the PSAP used a dedicated liaison line for pier incidents rather than pushing those contacts through 911. We are still above the 2024-Q4 low point, so the right posture is steady confidence with continued verification.
periods.recommendations: Keep the event liaison line in the special-event permit conditions and require after-action call-volume counts from event organizers within five business days. Extend the non-emergency-number signage package to beach lots B, C, and F before the next visitor season. Have supervisors compare abandoned-call timestamps against CAD event IDs for waterfront incidents to confirm the 0.3-point improvement is tied to the controls, not just lower call pressure.

periods.analysis: The abandonment rate reached 3.6% in 2025-Q4, down 0.6 percentage points from 4.2%, remaining green and comfortably within the <=5.0% target. This continues the recovery from the 2025-Q2 high point and shows the operation translated lessons from summer into routine practice. The full console call-back workflow, the fall staffing bid, and the cross-trained cohort PSAP-25B gave supervisors more options during storm watches and holiday retail peaks. The result protects community trust because the improvement is repeatable and tied to named procedures, not luck.
periods.recommendations: Lock the full console call-back workflow into the PSAP quality assurance manual and audit ten abandoned-call records per watch each month. Preserve the cross-trained PSAP-25B coverage in the 2026 staffing plan, especially for storm-watch activation and retail district weekends. Use the Q4 3.6% performance as the benchmark for winter operations while still keeping the formal target at <=5.0%.

periods.analysis: In 2026-Q1 the rate was 3.7%, up 0.1 percentage points from 3.6%, and remained green under the <=5.0% target. That is essentially stable performance through a quarter with two coastal wind advisories and several mutual-aid fire dispatches. The CAD upgrade patch on HB-CAD-7 did not create a measurable abandonment issue, which reflects disciplined cutover testing and floor-walker support during the first week. The small increase is a reminder to keep procedural checks in place, but it does not indicate deterioration.
periods.recommendations: Continue the CAD floor-walker model for the next two minor releases, with one supervisor and one vendor technician assigned during the first 48 hours. Sustain the monthly QA sample and add a specific field noting whether any abandoned call occurred during CAD latency or radio-channel congestion. Keep the staffing and call-back procedures unchanged for now, because the 3.7% result shows the current controls are working.

periods.analysis: The 2026-Q2 abandonment rate increased to 4.5%, up 0.8 percentage points from 3.7%, while still meeting the green <=5.0% target. This matches the 2025-Q2 level, so the seasonal pattern is now clear: late spring events, beach openings, and construction-related calls compress the answer window. Harborview remains inside standard, but we are again operating close enough to the threshold that the community would notice any further slippage. The PSAP handled the load, and the concern is managed, but the next quarter needs an explicit peak-season control plan.
periods.recommendations: Activate the peak-season PSAP plan by June 1 each year, including one added 1400-2200 position on event Fridays, beach-opening weekends, and Route 6 or Seawall Drive construction closure days. Expand public messaging for the non-emergency line through beach parking receipts, hotel concierge packets, and construction-alert texts. Set a supervisor trigger at 4.7% month-to-date abandonment so staffing, call-back scripts, and event liaison channels are adjusted before the measure risks moving out of green.

periods.analysis: 911 call abandonment rose from 4.5% to 5.3%, exceeding the 5.0% ceiling. Peak-season demand has narrowed dispatch capacity; the result does not establish that any proposed staffing or call-routing change has been tested or adopted.
periods.recommendations: Review peak-hour staffing and abandonment by shift, then test the dispatch protocol before deciding whether added coverage or a longer-term coordination option is warranted. Regional dispatch staffing reports elsewhere are context, not evidence of a Harborview solution.
